Commentary.Commentary: The Aussies have to come hard and strong if they have to go for the win. As of now, to draw this match looks a great option. Australia have not chased a 250-plus target in last four matches in Asia. Can they amend it here? Join us for the chase in a bit.

There it is finally, the hosts have declared at 347/8 and they feel the target of 324 is good enough to put Australia in to bat. de Silva and Lakmal did well to add a few quick runs in this early morning session. Australia did their best to delay the process with their too many mini drinks session.
Full toss around off, driven through mid off for a single. SRI LANKA DECLARE WITH A LEAD OF 323!
FIVE NO BALLS! BEAMER! It is a massive full toss above the stumps. de Silva lets it through and it gets past the keeper as well and goes to the fence at fine leg.
Yorker on off, de Silva digs it out well.

NOT OUT! Fuller ball outside off, pushed to the covers for a couple. Starc chases it down and throws it at the batsman's end and the keeper removes the bails. The umpire asks for the third umpire to step in. The replays show that de Silva slid in well in time and is adjudged safe.
de Silva pulls that short delivery again through to the leg side for a single.
Length ball around off, defended from within the crease.
FOUR! Short ball outside off, Silva pulls it through mid-wicket. He is able to find the gap and the ball crosses the ropes.
Length ball outside off, Silva opens the face of his bat and looks to guide it to third man. It goes to Smith at the slips and is stopped.
FOUR! de Silva marks it well! Fuller ball outside off, de Silva comes down the track and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.

NOT OUT! Length ball outside off, de Silva plays it to mid-wicket and the batsmen decide to go for a brace. The fielder collects it and makes a direct throw at the bowler's end. The umpire refers it upstairs and the replays show that Lakmal dived in time to be well inside the crease when the bails went flying.
Sri Lanka are going strong with their lead...
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, Lakmal looks to pull it but gis hit on the elbow and the ball bounces right next to his feet and goes to the keeper.
Starc is on with a new pair of boots. Here we go again.
Starc looks in some pain, maybe his toe needs some attention. He is taking his time to resume... Mini drinks on field as of now.

FOUR! WHAT A BEAUTY! Full around off, Lakmal waits back in the crease and drives it straight as an arrow past the stumps at the bowler's end. The ball goes down the ground and across the boundary line.
Fullish ball outside off, de Silva drives it through the covers for a single. SL take a lead of 300 with that!
FOUR BYES! Very wide down the leg side, the ball angles in. The keeper dives to his left but is still too far away to stop it. The ball keeps going behind the stumps and finds the fence.
Length ball outside off and angled away, de Silva shoulders his arms.
Fuller ball on leg, de Silva nudges it to deep fine leg .
Bouncer! Lakmal ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Length ball and angled in, Lakmal misses his shot and is hit on the thigh pad. There is a brief appeal but the ball was going down leg.
Back of a length ball outside off, Lakmal looks to cut it and edges it to the man at point.
Maiden Test fifty for Dhananjaya de Silva.
Length ball on off, de Silva works it to the leg side for a single.
FOUR! SLAPPED! Good length delivery outside off, de Silva smashes it over the bowler's head and the ball goes all the way for a boundary at long off. Good start for SL!
Bouncer down leg, that one went miles above de Silva. He doesn't even bother to move and the ball goes above him! The square leg umpire  signals a wide.
Hazlewood finds the landing area a bit uncomfortable and asks for hammering work to be done. Yesterday Nathan Lyon was in action for the same.
Length ball outside off, blocked off the front foot to point.
JOSH HAZLEWOOD to bowl from the other end.
Fuller ball on  middle and leg, worked to mid-wicket.
Length ball around off, Lakmal defends it off the back foot with hard hands.
Bouncer! Lakmal ducks to let it through.
Starc from over the wicket now, bowls a short ball outside off, Lakmal is all watchful and leaves it for the keeper.
Fuller on the pads, tucked to mid-wicket.
Starc starts steaming in from around the wicket with a full toss, de Silva drives it through covers straightaway for a single.

The players and umpires are out in the middle for the morning session. DHANANJAYA DE SILVA and SURANGA LAKMAL will take their places at the centre while MITCHELL STARC will begin the bowling proceedings.

Pitch Report - Russel Arnold reckons that there are plenty of roughs patches. The ball needs to hit the rough patch to get dividends. Also talks about playing reverse sweep as the best option. Ends by saying that the pitch looks a bit turning and the team batting on day 5 will have to bat hard and tough to see through.

Australia did their best in restricting the Lankans but didn't have much success in stemming the leaking of runs. The tourists are definitely up for a challenge  and will look to strike back hard today. With the game on the line, this is going to be an enthralling competition between bat and ball. Sit back, relax and stay tuned, as we provide you with the commentary of today's action.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final day of the 3rd Test between Sri Lanka and Australia. The hosts have managed to extend their lead to 288 runs after a powerful knock of 115 by Kaushal Silva. The groundwork set, Sri Lanka will most likely look to cross the 300-run mark before an early declaration.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

Australia tried their best to pick up wickets but got lucky only thrice in this session. The rest of the time, the hosts played freely and made a run feast. After being in a such commanding position, Sri Lanka may look to declare and allow the tourists to go for the chase. Day 5 will have minimum 90 overs and an ideal possibility for both the sides to go for a win. So what do we have in store for tomorrow? Will it be an overnight declaration ? Or will the hosts like to add few 50-odd runs and then allow Australia for the same? Do join us for the 5th and final day of this 3-match Test series at 1000 IST. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Sri Lanka have taken the anchor deep in this session. 100-plus runs are scored and just at the loss of 3 wickets. At tea the hosts were at 187/5 and then they simply carried on in a great fashion. The duo of Chandimal and Silva played handy innings and stitched a stand of 90 runs when the former got out after his steady innings. The sensational Silva didn't dither and scored his 3rd Test century to strengthen their lead. After his wicket, de Silva kept ticking the scoreboard to get the lead close to 300-run mark. Which should give them a psychological advantage.
Low full toss around off, de Silva drives it through mid off for a single. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 4! SRI LANKA LEAD BY 288 RUNS!

It goes past the left of the keeper in the blink of an eye, and to Steven Smith behind him at first slip. SL lead by 253 runs.

Chandimal off his back foot looks to tuck it to the leg side but misses the line of the ball completely. The umpire says not out but Australia reviews it. The replays show that the ball pitches in line and go on to hit the stumps. The impact is in line so umpire has overturned his decision. With that the stand of 90 runs is broken too. The hard-fought innings of Dinesh is over.
LBW appeal for Chandimal has been given not out by the umpire. Australia have decided to review it.

Welcome to the final session of the day. The players and umpires are back on for the final session. KAUSHAL SILVA and DINESH CHANDIMAL will resume their partnership and JOSH HAZLEWOOD will start the bowling.
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

The Aussies struck back with a turner from Nathan Lyon being gloved to Steven Smith at the slips. That spelt the end for Mathews. The tourists are now alternating between a spin and pace attack. Dinesh Chandimal is playing his supporting role to the hilt, allowing Silva to add to the lead. Sri Lanka have a 163-run lead with five wickets in hand and the pair look well-settled and Australia will be keen to shake things up when they get back. Join us shortly for the final session.

A session that is marginally in the favour of the hosts. It's been a challenging one and Sri Lanka  had to struggle for every run out there. They persevered at it and brought up 78 runs in 28 overs, a respectable accomplishment on a day 4 pitch. Kaushal Silva scored a gritty half-century and soon after, he and partner Angelo Mathews brought up a 50-run stand.
Fuller ball in the slot for Silva, he negotiates it well. THAT'S TEA ON DAY 4!
Length ball, width on offer, Silva itching for that one as he tries to drive it through covers. Gets beaten in the end.

Welcome back for the post-Lunch session. Kaushal Silva and Angelo Mathews will continue to bat. Jon Holland to bowl. Let's play...
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Australia have been prolific this morning with the ball and their fielding. They gave runs but took all important wickets of the players as they were off to a good start. As of now the hosts lead by 85 runs. Will Sri Lanka be able to resist the bowling of the Aussies and set up a good target? Or will it be a paltry target by them. Do join us in a bit for the mid-day session to find out.

Australia have certainly fought this session out with their fiery bowling this morning. The overnight batsman, Karunaratne was given out because of his stroll in a park approach and was stumped by Nevill. After that Perera was  unlucky too, to be given out by the TV umpire for a catch appeal. Mendis was a  real wicket in a dead plumb off Starc bowling. This session was all about events, lots of stroke-making, runs-scoring and tumble of wickets few earned and few harsh ones. Nevertheless, that's the nature of Test cricket.

Pitch Report - The pitch has rough patches on either end and the question is, can the bowlers bowl in this areas. It looks a dead pitch and only the spinners can be benefited. The orthodox spinner against right-handers and the chinaman against the left-handers will be a great test of character. The players will have to show temperament and composure to win it from here, reckons Russel Arnold.

The morning session shall be crucial to the hosts as well. They suffered an early loss when Mitchell Starc removed Dilruwan Perera and will hope to get a solid partnership going. It's going to be an important day for both sides so stay tuned for all the action.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the 3rd Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club, Colombo. Australia fought hard yesterday to wipe out the deficit, mainly due to a brilliant 246-run partnership between Steven Smith and Shaun Marsh. They will be eager to keep up their performance, and look to wipe out the Lankans as early as possible.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Join us tomorrow at 1000 IST for all the action on Day 4. It is going to be an interesting and entertaining day of cricket as it will show us in which direction the match is heading. Till then, take care! Cheers!

Herath once again was the star performer with a 6-wicket haul. After bowling out Australia for 379, they trailed by 24 runs. To see off the last few overs, they sent in Dilruwan Perera to open. But the plan failed as he fell to Starc. Now, the Lankans are slightly on the back foot and will look to bat better tomorrow to post a challenging target for the Aussies.

End of the third day's play and Australia after picking a wicket in the little period before stumps have their noses just in front. The day started with Australia being 214 runs behind and ended with them leading by 2 runs. The overnight pair of Smith and Shaun Marsh added up 246 runs for the second wicket, giving the visitors a perfect start. After their departure, wickets started tumbling down with Mitchell Marsh staying out in the middle and scoring a fifty.
